newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk Rant aims 11 trln lira 97 turnover.
newsitem.headline: Turk Rant aims 11 trln lira 97 turnover.

text.p: Turkish leasing firm Rant Finansal Kiralama A.S. targets 11 trillion lira of turnover in 1997, up sharply from three trillion last year, general manager Bulent Tasar said.
"We had aimed two trillion lira of turnover for 1996 and made three trillion lira. This year the company target is 11 trillion lira. I believe it will be reached," Tasar told Reuters in an interview.
Tasar expects to attain a high profitability in 1997 unless there is a deterioration in Turkish politics which could worsen the country's economic ills.
Rant leasing posted 223.3 billion lira of net profits in 1996, up 127 percent from 1995. It shares closed at 3,650 lira on the Istanbul Stock Exchange on Thursday, versus 3,600 lira.
Fifty percent of the company's leasing turnover was made in machinery, 17 percent in computers and 13 percent in commercial vehicles last year.
Tasar said the change in the company's ownership in 1996 had a positive effect on the company.

"Sparx group formed by Japanese Nomura securities acquired 22.5 percent share and (private) Tekstilbank sold its stake," he said, adding that medium and long-term far east funds secured through its new shareholder helped the company's growth.
Tasar said talks were underway with the World Bank and its affiliate the International Finance Corporation (IFC) in an attempt to get medium and long-term loans.
"The talks are progressing positively and apart from that, opportunities to borrow in the medium and long-term from international markets are growing," he said.
